subject.title: fix: QueuedFileWriter silently swallows all write errors

question: Should optional `QueuedFileWriter` diagnostic sinks warn when mkdir or append fails, and what bounded/redacted warning policy should be accepted?
rationale: The source behavior is clear, but the reporter narrowed impact to optional diagnostics and the safe user-facing policy is not settled by existing code or docs.

options.title: Add bounded diagnostic warning
options.body: Approve a deduped or periodic non-fatal warning/debug signal for consecutive write failures that avoids sensitive path or payload leakage.

options.title: Keep silent best-effort writes
options.body: Treat diagnostic JSONL persistence as intentionally best-effort and close the issue without adding operator-facing noise.

options.title: Refresh or close the linked fork PR
options.body: Ask a maintainer to decide whether the conflicting fork PR should be sponsored into the target repo, replaced, or closed before implementation proceeds.

recommendation.title: Add bounded diagnostic warning
recommendation.body: Approve a deduped or periodic non-fatal warning/debug signal for consecutive write failures that avoids sensitive path or payload leakage.

likelyOwner.reason: The shared writer and its diagnostic callers appear to originate from `steipete`'s commit history, making this the strongest routing signal for the warning-policy choice.
